hero.headline: St. Lucie County offering free rip current safety demonstrations at three pools this summer
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation will host three free sessions using a rip current simulation machine to teach proper escape techniques in a controlled environment.
hero.body:
St. Lucie County residents and visitors can learn life-saving skills through free rip current safety demonstrations at local public pools this summer. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using a new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. She explained that the demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water that flow away from shore and are capable of quickly pulling swimmers away from the beach. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States. Many swimmers make a critical mistake when caught in a rip current by trying to swim directly back to shore, which often leads to dangerous exhaustion. The proper technique is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle.

The county has scheduled three free demonstrations this summer. The first will take place on July 19 from 1 to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool with registration required and attendance limited to 50 participants. The second demonstration will be held on July 28 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event. This session requires no registration and operates on a first-come, first-served basis. The final demonstration will occur on August 16 from 1 to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants.

The hands-on training aims to build swimmer confidence and prepare participants for real ocean conditions before they head to area beaches. The rip current simulation machine provides a controlled setting where people can practice the techniques needed to escape dangerous currents without the risks associated with actual ocean conditions. For more information about the rip current safety demonstrations, residents can contact St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation.

cards.headline: Suspect identified in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher on Essex Drive
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified the suspect in a fatal shooting that killed a 66-year-old Fort Pierce man on Tuesday afternoon. Andre Leonard Barnes, an art teacher for St. Lucie County, died at a local hospital after being shot with a rifle at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive. The suspect has been identified as Dale A. Mincey, who remains in custody on unrelated felony warrants from Broward County.

Deputies responded to the home around 3:30 p.m. Tuesday after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When they arrived, law enforcement learned that one man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes was transported to a local hospital, where he died from his injuries. Authorities have not released details about what led to the shooting or the relationship between Barnes and the suspect.

Mincey is currently being held on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker, according to the sheriff's office. The homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to the investigation will be determined as the case progresses. Deputies said that based on information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident with no threat to the public.

The school district released a statement following Barnes's death, acknowledging his service as an art teacher in St. Lucie County. The sheriff's office said additional information will be released as it becomes available. The investigation continues as authorities work to determine what charges will be filed in connection with Barnes's death.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher shot and killed on Essex Drive, suspect identified
cards.teaser: A 66-year-old Fort Pierce art teacher died Tuesday after being shot with a rifle at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive in St.
cards.body:
A 66-year-old man was shot and killed Tuesday at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive in St. Lucie County. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. The victim, identified as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce, was taken to a local hospital where he died. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie County Schools, and the district released a statement following his death.

The suspect in the homicide investigation has been identified as Dale A. Mincey, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. The homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Deputies said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce overhauls development process after multiple waterfront property lawsuits
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of Little J.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce city commissioners voted unanimously Monday night to reject a settlement offer from Kevin Keene, who is suing the city over its handling of Little Jim's Bait & Tackle restaurant. The rejection means more taxpayer dollars will likely go toward defending the case. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the settlement wasn't practical, particularly a provision that would have required taxpayers to vote on future waterfront land decisions. "You can't wait for an election or fund a special election every time you want to do something on city-owned property that's waterfront," Broderick said. Keene told WPTV he will continue the litigation and wants transparency, not money. Broderick said he also feels the lawsuit doesn't have any merit.

The Little Jim case is at least the fourth waterfront property dispute and the second to result in a lawsuit. In 2023, King's Landing developer Dale Matteson threatened legal action after claiming the city sold him buildable land filled with old power plant concrete. In 2024, Fisherman's Wharf developer Chris Shelli filed suit after state records showed the city promised property it didn't own. This year, the city became responsible for nearly $200,000 in unpaid rent tied to Crabby's Waterfront Restaurant. Broderick acknowledged the problems in a sit-down interview with WPTV. "I'm not going to say it's managed poorly. I'm going to say it's not being managed, and that's an issue I take very seriously," Broderick said. The city is creating a new real estate management position to track leases, rent payments, and waterfront properties.

cards.headline: Vero Beach condo waste management fees jump 93% under new county contract
cards.body:
Indian River County condo owners are seeing waste management fees nearly double after a new contract with Waste Management began in October 2025. Thomas Clark, a Vero Beach condo owner, brought his concerns to WPTV during a Let's Hear It community meetup, reporting his monthly waste management fees had jumped from $11 to $21.

WPTV Anchor Mike Trim brought these concerns directly to the Indian River County Department of Utility Services during a video conference meeting. The county explained the new contract raised average condo association waste management fees by roughly 93 percent. Clark told Trim he was not happy with the increase and suggested the county should help residents if the county made a mistake in the contract.

County officials said condo owners are receiving additional benefits under the new contract. Himanshu Mehta of the Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District explained that residents can now place bulk items near condo dumpsters, a service that was not previously available. Mehta and other county officials emphasized the importance of community involvement in public hearings, noting that this contract was approved during 2024 hearings.

Mehta said his team is available to meet with homeowners associations to explain the process in more detail. He stated that if Clark or his HOA wanted to invite county officials to a meeting, they would be happy to send someone to go over the process. Residents can stay updated on Indian River County public hearings and find current recycling and garbage schedules on the county website.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Clerk's website goes down for hours, redirects visitors
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Clerk and Comptroller's website was down for hours Tuesday, redirecting visitors to another site before coming back online by about 1:30 p.m. Clerk and Comptroller Michelle Miller posted a video on social media Tuesday afternoon addressing the outage, assuring the public that no personal or confidential information was compromised or at risk. The clerk's office does not store sensitive personal information on the public-facing website, Miller said in the social media post. Miller said the website faced a temporary redirection issue caused by a third-party service provider.

WPTV reporter Tyler Hatfield went to the County Clerk's office in search of answers and spoke to Jose Clavijo, the agency's IT director. Clavijo said they received a report just before 8 a.m. that something was wrong with the county clerk's homepage. He said as soon as he identified the problem, he turned off the homepage immediately and started an investigation. Clavijo said getting the site fixed was the absolute highest priority.

WPTV asked the St. Lucie County Clerk's Office if it believed there was any suspicious activity about the incident, such as a hack. The clerk's office communications team said this was not a hack because there was not any personal information compromised. The office said residents could still access information and services on the website through direct links instead of using the homepage. Clavijo said payments, property fraud services, and all other services remained available. He said the main page was the only issue.

Clavijo said the office is working to prevent similar issues from happening again. He said as soon as they identify the exact issue, there will be a tremendous remediation. The website outage lasted several hours Tuesday morning before service was restored in the early afternoon. The clerk's office emphasized that despite the redirection problem, no sensitive data was at risk and most services remained accessible throughout the incident.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of August debut
cards.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The league also includes the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters.

The WPBL's debut season begins on Aug. 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. The league hopes to create a space for women's baseball players similar to the one the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League did 70 years ago. "This is just every little girl's dream to play professional baseball," Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March, "and now for us to actually be with each other, there's so much freedom and peace within it."

Each team identity holds a unique meaning. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. Their logo includes graphic lines surrounding a baseball, mimicking the speed of a fastball and resembling the New York skyline. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as "Firebelle," who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. Their logo fuses a bell with a phoenix. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the "Queen of the Diamond." The logo is a capital Q topped with four baseball diamonds.

The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist. Their logo is an osprey clasping a baseball bat in its talons. The league represents years of planning to establish professional opportunities for women in baseball, giving players a chance to compete at the highest level. With rosters finalized and team identities now revealed, the WPBL is set to make its debut next month in Illinois, marking a new chapter in women's professional sports.

hero.headline: Jensen Beach Park concession building and restrooms to be rebuilt by late 2027
hero.teaser: Jensen Beach Park beachgoers have been waiting for the rebuild of the park's restrooms and concession building since a fire destroyed them on New Year's Eve in December 2024.
hero.body:
The site where Jensen Beach Park's concession building and restrooms once stood is now an empty plot of land following a fire that destroyed the facility on New Year's Eve in December 2024. Beachgoer Gonda Ghebert reached out to WPTV's Let's Hear It inbox, writing that beachgoers are left with only one very small restroom facility to serve the entire beach. The situation has become increasingly unreasonable during weekends, holidays, and peak tourist season. Regular visitors say they miss both the restrooms and the cafe, with one beachgoer noting the location previously offered nice, clean facilities, showers, and the convenience of getting snacks and drinks right off the deck.

Kevin Abbate, Parks and Recreation director, said the permitting process takes time because the site sits on a protected dune and requires approval from the Department of Environmental Protection. That permit is currently in process. The design for the new 9,000 square foot Sea Turtle Beach Cafe is 80 percent complete. "It's about 15 feet in elevation, so there's a good seat for everyone, 100 seats and 33 at the bar," Abbate said.

The county says final funding is expected to be approved in September. They hope to start construction in early 2027 with a completion goal of late 2027, just in time for the winter season. The county told WPTV they do not have any plans for additional temporary restrooms or facilities in the meantime. Abbate said the wait will be worthwhile because doing the project correctly from the start will prevent problems later.

"We want to do it right. If we design it properly, when we get through construction, we'll have fewer issues, it'll be a much smoother process," Abbate said. Beachgoers say they are anxiously awaiting the construction. One visitor hopes the project moves very fast, while another expressed eagerness to see the bathrooms up and running again and called it nice to have another convenient spot at the beach.

cards.headline: US-Belgium World Cup match draws record 30 million viewers on Fox Sports
cards.teaser: Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, with viewership peaking at 36 million during the second half.
cards.body:
Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported. According to Fox, the match drew more than 30 million viewers. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of Monday's match. The United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast. Interest in Monday's match intensified after FIFA announced that Folarin Balogun would be eligible to play against Belgium despite receiving a red card last week against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said its World Cup broadcasts have generated significant interest beyond U.S. matches. The network said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: United States eliminated from World Cup after 4-1 loss to Belgium in Seattle
cards.teaser: Belgium knocked the U.S. out of the World Cup in the round of 16 for the second time in 12 years, winning 4-1 at Lumen Field as Charles De Ketelaere scored twice.
cards.body:
The United States' hopes for a deep World Cup run at home ended when Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium expose the Americans' defensive liabilities in a 4-1 win Monday night that earned a quarterfinal berth. American defenders were at fault in a pair of first-half goals and goalkeeper Matt Freese's gaffe gave the Red Devils a third early in the second half. Second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku added Belgium's final goal in the third minute of stoppage time before a crowd of 66,925 at Lumen Field.

Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 midway through the first half with his second free kick goal of the tournament, but the Americans conceded just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff. American star Christian Pulisic could only watch from the bench after injuring his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt. Pulisic favored his foot after that and was replaced seven minutes later. Seeking its first World Cup title, Belgium knocked the U.S. out in the round of 16 for the second time in 12 years and extended its unbeaten streak to 18 games. The Red Devils play 2010 champion Spain on Friday at Inglewood, California, for a semifinal berth against France or Morocco.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi leads Argentina to 3-2 comeback victory over Egypt in World Cup round of 16
cards.teaser: Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and Argentina rallied from a two-goal deficit with 11 minutes left to defeat Egypt 3-2 and advance to the World Cup quarterfinals.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and led Argentina to an improbable 3-2 victory over Egypt on Tuesday despite trailing by two with only 11 minutes of regulation time to play. The defending champions will next face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri. Messi, who was in tears after the final whistle, scored his record-extending 21st goal at the World Cup in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete one of the great World Cup comebacks. Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute.

Argentina had trailed 2-0 on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico. Messi also missed a chance in the first half when his penalty kick was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir. He later hit the post when the score was 1-0. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962. For much of the game, it looked like it would be a painful exit for the 39-year-old Messi in what might be the last of his six World Cups. Ibrahim gave Egypt a surprising lead in the 15th minute when he got ahead of Lisandro Martinez to meet Marwan Attia's cross and head the ball into the bottom corner.

cards.headline: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
cards.teaser: The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 LA Olympics.
cards.body:
The IOC advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The move was expected since the International Olympic Committee advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity. The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension, imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine, no longer applied, the IOC said.

Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem. That decision will come at an appropriate time, it said. The next Olympic competition is the 2026 Youth Summer Games in Dakar, Senegal opening Oct. 31. The IOC said it will continue to not organize IOC events in Russia or invite Russian government or state officials to its events.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. announced the return of the Treasure Coast Seafood Festival to Vero Beach for its 18th year this November. The annual festival draws visitors throughout the region for seafood vendors, entertainment and family activities.

The event is organized by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc., which has coordinated the festival in Vero Beach for nearly two decades. The festival features local and regional seafood vendors along with live music and activities for attendees.

The festival has become a signature autumn event for Indian River County residents and visitors. Organizers use the event to showcase coastal cuisine and entertainment while supporting local businesses and community organizations.

Specific dates, venue location and vendor information for the November 2026 festival will be released by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. in the coming weeks. The event typically attracts thousands of visitors to Vero Beach each year.

The second demonstration will be held on July 28 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event. This session requires no registration and operates on a first-come, first-served basis. The final demonstration will occur on August 16 from 1 to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants.

The hands-on training aims to build swimmer confidence and prepare participants for real ocean conditions before they head to area beaches. The rip current simulation machine provides a controlled setting where people can practice the techniques needed to escape dangerous currents without the risks associated with actual ocean conditions. For more information about the rip current safety demonstrations, residents can contact St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher shot and killed on Essex Drive, suspect identified
cards.teaser: A 66-year-old Fort Pierce art teacher died Tuesday after being shot with a rifle at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive in St.
cards.body:
A 66-year-old man was shot and killed Tuesday at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive in St. Lucie County. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. The victim, identified as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce, was taken to a local hospital where he died. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie County Schools, and the district released a statement following his death.

The suspect in the homicide investigation has been identified as Dale A. Mincey, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. The homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Deputies said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident and there is no threat to the public.

hero.headline: Vero Beach condo waste management fees jump 93% under new county contract
hero.body:
Indian River County condo owners are seeing waste management fees nearly double after a new contract with Waste Management began in October 2025. Thomas Clark, a Vero Beach condo owner, brought his concerns to WPTV during a Let's Hear It community meetup, reporting his monthly waste management fees had jumped from $11 to $21.

WPTV Anchor Mike Trim brought these concerns directly to the Indian River County Department of Utility Services during a video conference meeting. The county explained the new contract raised average condo association waste management fees by roughly 93 percent. Clark told Trim he was not happy with the increase and suggested the county should help residents if the county made a mistake in the contract.

County officials said condo owners are receiving additional benefits under the new contract. Himanshu Mehta of the Indian River County Solid Waste Disposal District explained that residents can now place bulk items near condo dumpsters, a service that was not previously available. Mehta and other county officials emphasized the importance of community involvement in public hearings, noting that this contract was approved during 2024 hearings.

Mehta said his team is available to meet with homeowners associations to explain the process in more detail. He stated that if Clark or his HOA wanted to invite county officials to a meeting, they would be happy to send someone to go over the process. Residents can stay updated on Indian River County public hearings and find current recycling and garbage schedules on the county website.
